TAG WITHHELD AGAIN, FOLLOWING THE 17:30 RUN RATHER THAN RE-OPENING THE QUESTION. The holds are unchanged, this run opened no new section 5 case, and nothing was blocked by them - the stamp committed cleanly. The 17:30 run broke a run of 141 identical tagged DMs and recorded its reasoning: runbook section 4a says to tag every unanswered hold, the same section warns that a mention on every quiet heartbeat trains the reader to ignore it, and the scheduled task prompt says plainly not to tag quiet no-change messages. On a 145-hour-old hold the hourly repeat has stopped working as a notification. Flipping the tag back on this hour, with nothing new to report, would be the worst of both - it would read as new urgency where there is none, and the October post-mortem's finding was precisely that successive DMs disagreeing with each other is what destroys their signal. So this run sent the no-change heartbeat shape, untagged, with all seven holds named, their age stated and the consolidated A/B question still in the message. Nothing about the holds is decided either way and no figure is affected. It remains Arushi's call: if she would rather have the tag back every hour, the next run should resume it.
